what: Second and last adversarial review of pull request 5 of BRIEF-canon.md (the absorption shimmer; item 6). The same three lenses as round 1, each checking round 1's fixes first: design and accessibility (the glow's placement on both pictures, measured against the image files; the tile and the screen-reader tree; reduced motion), copy (every changed sentence on the page, the cards, the README and the pull request, against the engine and each other), and code (the tally against the engine's runs, round 1's reverts, the tests and their mutants: 57 engine, 20 page and 17 ladder mutants run by the code lens). Reviewed at f6d20c3. Each report was reproduced by a skeptic with its own script: 9 findings, all confirmed, all minor, none merged. Fixed as the session lead decided: with the skeptics' better fixes, except where an outcome says otherwise (design: the crest tips measured from the image file, all eleven, not the skeptic's six points copied; copy-4 followed into the game of catch, where the same unlabelled upper bound was found; code-4: the effort read from the page's own slider in one load, in place of a second, custom-effort load); every figure worked out in the engine (scratchpad pr5/r2fix/js/figs2.js, at f6d20c3 and now: only the arm-wrestling pin and the three fast catches move) or read on the page, never copied by hand. One fix needed a reading canon doesn't settle: whose take an arm-wrestling pin's slam is (the winner's: decision 25, item 12 on the owner's list, in the README and the description alike). Each fix was reverted on its own in a scratch copy and its check seen failing (scratchpad pr5/r2fix/js/revert2.py and revert2b.py, results in pr5/r2fix/revert2-results.json: 15 reverts, 4 in the engine and 11 on the page and in the cards; the README and description fixes have copy checks, pr5/r2fix/js/docs2.py, that fail on the old texts). Every earlier mutant was re-run on the fixed tree: 232 (round 2's reviewers' 93 and skeptics' 7, the copy lens's 11 reverts of round 1's fixes, round 1's 17 reverts, 7 page and 15 engine mutants, the engine stage's 53 and the page stage's 29; 12 patterns later code had moved were followed into it). 218 fail the test they were written against; two more fail another test of the line (N25, a leg's drag credited to the catcher, fails the --pr5 block's duo-who; the skeptics' mutA and mutB together fail section 9j); twelve are equivalent: N02 and N05 (the stomp's and the jump's figures exist only with their power on), N04 (exactly Mach 1, which no dial lands on), N15 (Collide's hit and stop exist only in a carried hit), N28 (no part's input is ever negative), N30 (no game-of-catch leg's full-drag flight times out: 2,649 legs searched, scratchpad pr5/r2fix/js/n30.js), N43 and round 1's EM 11 (a flight past 1% of light speed never lands), round 1's EM 09 (hitsGround.kept is set exactly when hitsGround.own is), the engine stage's nan-guard (one of two NaN guards), and the ladder's L13 (the flare step's roughness is its own rung's either way) and L15 (the strength below the floor is clamped to 0 anyway). Four the reviewers had left surviving now fail: N29 (an unbounded catch beside an unbounded drag: section 9j) and L01 (a tie taking the upper step: test/ladder.js's new tie check), which the code lens had judged equivalent, and P21 (the return leg rebuilt as a fastball: a lob's round trip in duo-tiles, added after the run and checked again). With every power off every engine result is byte-identical (powers.js part 1, its fixture unchanged). node test/shots.js --pr5 alone: 71.7 s and 71.2 s before the fixes, 79.4 s, 76.4 s and 79.4 s after (23 checks, from 19). After the fixes, the full Rex lab test line, one test at a time in the 4-CPU cloud sandbox, and all pass: build-data.py and build.js; calibration.js all checks passed (109 s); presence.js 383 checks (45 s); shots.js 85 checks, no problems (853 s); powers.js 221 of 221 (227 s; section 9 now 40 checks, was 36); ladder.js 579 of 579 (1 s; was 578); sweep.js 7,776 contexts with no NaN or negative output (524 s). The review rounds are complete.
